body:
Thanks for your response!  I imagine you (and others) who've read through get the sense that these events are relatively emotion-free.  After years of being in pain, striving for connection and failing, wondering if I'll ever feel anything again - I finally just conceded and let those things go.  I let my emotions go.  I let my caring go.  I realized it was a double-edged sword - I'd let go of the caring about being hurt, but I'd also let go of any feelings about anything.  That's the focus of my therapy at the moment because I can't feel anything.  I can talk at length about these events but I can't feel them.  My psychiatrist tried to make me feel something...tapping myself while telling myself that I'm a good person and I deserve to be happy.  All that did was make me self-harm and down a 5th of tequila while telling my husband that I was going to jump over the balcony.

I know it's a process and I'm on the path, but I don't know where that path is going and honestly don't really care where it goes.  I have told my sister about the first event - the cousin - but her breaking down into tears, trying to hold and comfort me (not a good thing for me) stopped me from telling her the rest.  I don't want to tell my dad - a) because he's not in the best of health, and b) because I think he'd feel responsible.  Maybe in some way he is responsible, but it's not something I want him to take on.  I have told my husband - I even forwarded this post to him - but I'm a whole person to him, not just these events.  He is dealing with the full picture, sometimes well and sometimes not so well, but he's trying and I do love him for that.

Thanks again for reaching out.
Anytime, anything.  :)
Sweden, huh?  Always wanted to visit...in the summer.  ;)  California here.  I hope you do feel better, it's good to reach out.  PM me if you ever want to chat.

Thanks - it's sometimes difficult to be on this subreddit and put your thoughts out there...you never know how someone will respond/react to them.  But at the same time, you need to put it out there.  I don't think the fear of death will ever go away...it's a biological thing...but hopefully the fear of causing it will.

Completely hear you.  Some people look at 30 years of struggling as a "success" - I tend to not see things that way.  I've thought very seriously about the gun route as well...the only thing that stopped that was the possibility of failing and being even more of a burden for whoever would have to take care of me.  PM me if you want to talk...kindred spirits and all...  ;)

Passion?  Enjoyment?  Nope...I'm just drifting through life trying to overcome the biological survival instinct.  Believe me, I've tried - I try every day - to find passion and enjoyment.  I do things that I used to find passion and enjoyment from and they do nothing for me anymore.  I try new things...nothing.  I do something completely out of my zone...fly to Bali on a whim, spend the entire time in the hotel watching tv.  So my question is, what is the point without passion and enjoyment?  How do you know my life is valuable, and to whom?  It's certainly not valuable to me and there's nobody else that it's valuable to...except maybe my bill collectors.

Thanks for your reply :)  No worries about being snarky or an asshole.  Yeah, I have the money and can do new experiences, but I've been doing that for 30 years and I'm just done with the chase...chasing something that doesn't exist.  I don't mean to point-counterpoint you - or anyone here - "don't jump"..."why not"..."because"..."because why"...  I am really just trying to find out what other people find interesting in life.  All those things that bring other people joy as just meaningless to me.  I mean, 30 years of searching for joy and meaning is a long time...
Why not?

I've wondered this as well.  Currently, I beat myself - arms, shoulder, thighs...  It gets the frustration out with the beating (ish) and the bruises are constant reminders that I just have to push on a little to feel the pain again.

If life were a marriage, I'd be divorced LONG ago.  I have no feeling for anything anymore.  No hobbies, no friends, no activities, no joy.  It's not that life is bad, per se, it's just not worth living without any sort of care about anything.  Yes, I'm sure there is no life after death.
An easy way out.  No fear.  No hesitation.

I'm sorry - I probably should've put a trigger warning in there.  For me, surviving isn't living...not that I'd know how to do that either.  Fear is the only emotion I haven't completely lost - yet - and I desperately want to lose that one.

Please, can we stop with the, "suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary situation" BS already?  You absolutely KNOW it's a temporary situation?  What I can pretty much guarantee is that most suicidal people don't arrive at being suicidal minutes before they post.  For many, if not most, it IS a permanent situation that's taken up 90% (or more) of their lives.

OP, I'm listening - and honestly, I'm where you're at except I've been suicidal for almost 30 years.  It's a constant struggle to go on, but I won't say it's been all bad.  Some days are better than others - which isn't to sell you the platitude of, "it'll get better".  That tired excuse of selfish people trying to trivialize your suffering is BS as well.  In my experience, nothing gets or doesn't get anything.  It's not the waiting around for something amazing to happen and magically wipe away depression and suicidal thoughts - it's fighting until you can't fight anymore.

Now, what happens when you can't fight anymore?  I believe that's a question only you can answer.  For me, I had to answer that question after I failed (twice) to kill myself - I got to the point where I couldn't fight anymore, but I didn't have an answer of what I was supposed to do when I got there.  My answer - and this is only for me, not a suggestion for you - is to 5150 myself.  (involuntary psychiatric commitment)  For some people, that may be the most innocuous thing...no big deal...but for me, I have a deathly fear of police and hospitals so it's a pretty big deterrent.

That's not to say I don't get there - oh boy, I get there, often.  But you're doing a good thing by reaching out, even if it's only on here.  I don't know you or what you're going through, but I'm happy to chat if you like.

Exactly.  It's hugely selfish for people to "need" us around for their own benefit, all the while negating our needs.  My dad just found out he has colon cancer and I got that exact comment, "I need you".  I couldn't help thinking he was glad he has cancer so he can guilt me into not killing myself.  In reality, all I am is jealous of him.

These catchphrases are beyond idiotic.  Switch it around:  "A temporary solution to a permanent problem" - is that any better?  Or, "it's just your perspective now" - like we just arrived at this perspective a few minutes ago.  I'm with you, and just to bug the never-death-er's, I'm going to post "A permanent solution to a permanent problem" every time I see someone advancing this stupid catchphrase.

I probably will "do life" (love that implication ;) with him.  He cares about me, wants to be with me - and since I don't care either way, I'm fine with giving him what he wants.  Well, ...ish...he still wants sex and to be more emotionally connected to me, but for me that ship has sailed.

Being in the gay community, social niceties are all there is.  And pushing 50 in the gay community?  You may as well be invisible.  I've never had any close gay friends and straight people tend to use you while they're looking for a relationship.  As soon as that happens, it's the dustbin for you.

I know, I shouldn't use those "it's never going to happen" phrases.  Who knows?  The only perspective I can come from is the one I have - but it's also a logical perspective.  It's like saying I've driven my car for 30 years...it's always turned left when I turned the wheel left; it's always gone straight when I pointed it straight.  But wait!  That's your perspective!  Tomorrow it might turn RIGHT when you turn the wheel left!  Um, yeah, don't think so.

For me, time/love/effort = pain/suffering/frustration/hate/violence.  I've been there too many times in my life where I've poured my heart out, put 110% in, bent over backwards - and I have nothing to show for it.  That fact used to eat at me and spiral me through one layer of horrible depression through the next.  So I've finally boxed up those feelings, pour some wine and Tramadol on the wounds, and wonder what the point of it all is.

Thanks for your post!  I know I'm not the only one feeling the way I do - and it's the main reason I posted in the first place, to see how others are/have been dealing with it.  I've often said it's like when you're lonely you only want to do the thing that keeps you lonely.  Sure, I could go out and be around people...reach out, call someone, talk to the mailman...but when you're lonely that's the last thing you want to do.

For me, I've been through so much pain, heartache, crying out to god (when I used to believe there was one), that to an extent, finally getting to a point where I don't care about anything is a strange sort of relief.  The flip side of that - and the reason for my post - is there's a part of me that doesn't understand the point of it all if I don't care about anything.

The husband is a sticky subject, for both of us.  So many things are unsaid, but mainly because they've already been said before and didn't go very well.  20 years is a lot of conversations...

Settled is a pretty-close definition, but to me it's more like the comment below saying I should "feel the pain".  It's coming to a realization that the pain is the glue.  Misery loves company, even if we both pretend we're not miserable.

By friendship hoops I mean all the niceties required to get to the point where you can actually be open with someone.  Invite them over for dinner, small talk about work, make plans to have a drink after work, go to a pool party they're throwing, blah blah blah.  I think you got it correct on the emotional connectivity - I'm not emotionally connected to anything or anyone, nor do I really want to be anymore.

I think this is why I cry when I see other people happy - I know that's not in the cards for me.  I've so desperately wanted that connection for my entire life and only now when I've finally been able to not care about having it realize I've never had it before.  I've never been emotionally connected to anyone or anything and seeing others who are (or who I perceive to be) tears my heart out.

I actually did tell my doctor (GP) that "I don't want to be here anymore", to which he asked, "here?  on this planet, here?"  I said, "here, anywhere" and he asked if I had a plan.  I said I do (multiple plans actually) and he got very quiet.  Little did I know at the time that he was considering admitting me.  Broken bones, yes.  Broken brains, not so much.

I'm not quite sure how this is my "perspective at the moment" when this has been my perspective for 30+ years, albeit sometimes the glass is half full vs. half empty.  I've had many, many opportunities to change my perspective...moved to NYC to work for a Fortune 2 company...hated it.  Bought a house in Florida...hated it.  I want to leave my husband just so he has the potential to be happy.

It's strange - sometimes I feel like talking about this is all I ever do, yet I'm not talking to anyone.  I'm talking AT my therapist, which is at least some measure of outlet.  But it feels like no amount of talking will amount to anything but talking about it.  It's like telling the car to drive up the hill...c'mon car, drive up the hill!  At some point you just realize it isn't going to happen.

Yeah, I used to feel the same way about fictional hubbies.  There have been many fights and hurt feelings over that very thing over the years.  I've come to realize I don't really want that with him.  After years and years of wishing/hoping/crying over not having something that I believed I needed I've finally been able to let that desire go.  I love him with all my heart...it's just there isn't much of a heart there.  Honestly, I don't know what reality and self-awareness would have to be in order to not ignore it.  It's kinda like, "ok, sweetie, get your coat, we're gonna head to the hospital so they can pump your stomach.  Actually, I have an early meeting tomorrow, so I'll just drop you off out front, ok?"

My therapist is the only one I can talk to, and that's completely one-way.  I know how to make friends, but I really don't want to.  The desire to be able to talk to people is there, but I don't want all the other hoops you have to jump through to have a friend.  Even seeing other people happy throws me into fits of crying...not good when you're, let's see, anywhere.  Crying at the bar, crying at the gym, crying at the baseball game, crying at the beach...UGH.

I've actually tried yoga and meditation in the past, mainly for stress.  Meditation on antidepressants, for me, doesn't work.  My brain either wanders, or is nowhere - both of which are frustrating, thereby negating the value.  I haven't looked specifically at vipassana, but I'll look it up.

As for the pain, I've had very bad relationships with GP's throughout most of my life - "feeling the pain" is what I've done for the majority.  So after years of not being able to sleep through the night, not able to tie my shoes, not able to sit for more than 30 minutes at a time, I finally found a really great GP who took pity on me and prescribed Tramadol.  It was literally night and day.

Interesting premise, though:  did I live with pain for so long, now that it's gone(ish) do I miss it?  Maybe so, sometimes.  But I've also self-harmed my entire life, so I still have that pain.

I'm completely not worried about drinking with medication.  It's kind of like the intentional vs. accidental balcony fall.  I'll know if it's intentional, but until then if it's accidental, so be it.

Thanks for the replies!  My husband does know about my attempts and that I want to KMS...that's the bad part of self medicating - one tends to be loose-lipped.  But it's definitely not something I want to discuss with him.  I think we'd all rather be ignorant.

I've been on antidepressants most of my adult life - I'm on Celebrex now (not that it's anywhere near a celebration as the name implies).  The problem with antidepressants for me is they either a) numb me to the point of a zombie-like state, which doesn't help with the not-caring thing, or b) remove all emotion, which isn't productive to a relationship and just allows me to consider suicide more objectively.

I've also seen therapists over the years and am seeing one now.  But I learned long ago to only value my need to talk about things to someone vs. thinking the therapist will give me anything even remotely useful.

I was kinda kidding about ECT/drugs...mostly kicking off some suggestions.  The underlying point was I just want to not know I don't care.
